abstract: We introduce Video Conferencing 1000 (VC-1K), an open-source test set comprising approximately 1,000 video sequences specifically designed for evaluating video processing and encoding pipelines in real-time communication (RTC) scenarios. Unlike existing test sets that primarily rely on studio-produced or screen content, VC-1K consists of user-generated video call content captured on consumer mobile devices under a wide variety of conditions. The dataset predominantly features talking-head sequences with distinct faces, but also includes a small subset of outward-facing, rear-camera videos without faces to reflect additional common RTC use cases. It spans a wide range of real-world variables including device type, lighting conditions, motion levels, indoor/outdoor environments, and demographic diversity. All video sequences are accompanied by synchronous audio to facilitate multimodal research. We detail the dataset's design methodology and statistical distribution, and demonstrate its utility through a comparative encoder evaluation of OpenH264, SVT-AV1, and libaom under constant bitrate (CBR) encoding at resolutions typical of RTC deployments. Furthermore, two super-resolution approaches, RealESRGAN and GFPGAN, are evaluated on VC-1K, highlighting the dataset as a useful benchmark for pre- and post-processing research. VC-1K is intended to serve as a publicly available dataset for the video RTC research community.

title: VC-1K: A Diverse Video Test Set for Real-Time Communication
